• Violation of forest laws in tribal areas.
• Salt satyagrahas across coastal regions.

Regional Movements
• Tamil Nadu – C. Rajagopalachari led salt march.
• North-West Frontier Province – Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Red Shirts movement).
• Maharashtra – forest satyagrahas.

PYQ Trap
• Red Shirts → Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

GOVERNMENT RESPONSE

Important Points
• Arrest of leaders including Gandhi.
• Use of force and repression.

GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (1931)

Introduction
• Agreement between Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin.

Features
• Suspension of Civil Disobedience Movement.
• Release of political prisoners.
• Participation of Congress in Round Table Conference.

PYQ Trap
• Gandhi attended Second Round Table Conference.

SECOND PHASE (1932–34)

Introduction
• Movement resumed after failure of Round Table Conference.

Features
• Reduced intensity.
• Continued repression by British.

Decline

Causes
• Government repression.
• Internal divisions.
• Lack of sustained mass participation.

Outcome
• Movement officially withdrawn in 1934.

PYQ Trap
• CDM had two phases (1930–31 and 1932–34).

SIGNIFICANCE

Political Impact
• Strengthened demand for independence.
• Demonstrated power of mass mobilization.

Social Impact
• Participation of women increased significantly.
• Spread of nationalist consciousness.

Economic Impact
• Boycott of British goods affected colonial economy.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Not fully nationwide.
• Limited participation from some regions.

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Important Points
• NCM → boycott (passive resistance).
• CDM → law breaking (active resistance).

PYQ Trap
• Key difference between NCM and CDM frequently asked.

Conclusion
• The Civil Disobedience Movement was a crucial stage in the freedom struggle.
• It intensified nationalist activities and brought India closer to independence.
Modern History.Round Table Conferences (1930–32):
ROUND TABLE CONFERENCES (1930–1932)

Introduction
• The Round Table Conferences were a series of three conferences held in London to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
• They were organized by the British Government to seek Indian cooperation in framing a new constitutional structure.

Background
• Failure of earlier reforms (Government of India Act, 1919).
• Pressure from Civil Disobedience Movement.
• Need for constitutional settlement between British and Indian leaders.

FIRST ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1930)

Introduction
• Held in London in November 1930.

Participation
• Attended by princes, minority groups, and British officials.
• Indian National Congress did not participate (leaders in jail due to CDM).

Outcome
• Discussion on federal structure.
• No concrete agreement reached.

PYQ Trap
• Congress absent in First Round Table Conference.

SECOND ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1931)

Introduction
• Held after Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

Participation
• Gandhi attended as the sole representative of Congress.

Key Issues
• Federal structure.
• Representation of minorities.

Outcome
• No agreement due to differences on minority representation.

PYQ Trap
• Gandhi attended only Second Round Table Conference.

THIRD ROUND TABLE CONFERENCE (1932)

Introduction
• Held after breakdown of talks.

Participation
• Congress again boycotted.

Outcome
• Limited participation.
• Led to further constitutional developments.

PYQ Trap
• Congress absent in First and Third RTC.

COMMUNAL AWARD (1932)

Introduction
• Announced by British PM Ramsay MacDonald.

Features
• Separate electorates for minorities including depressed classes.

Impact
• Led to Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar.

PYQ Trap
• Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with reserved seats.

SIGNIFICANCE

Political Impact
• Highlighted deep divisions among Indian leaders.
• Demonstrated British strategy of divide and rule.

Constitutional Impact
• Laid foundation for Government of India Act, 1935.

Limitations

Important Points
• Lack of consensus among Indian leaders.
• Congress not fully represented.

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Important Points
• First RTC → No Congress.
• Second RTC → Gandhi participated.
• Third RTC → No Congress again.

PYQ Trap
• Sequence and participation pattern is frequently asked.

Conclusion
• The Round Table Conferences failed to produce a consensus solution.
• However, they played a crucial role in shaping future constitutional developments leading to the Government of India Act, 1935.
Modern History.Cripps Mission (1942):
CRIPPS MISSION (1942)

Introduction
• The Cripps Mission was sent to India in March 1942 by the British Government during World War II.
• It was an attempt to secure Indian cooperation in the war effort by offering constitutional concessions.

Background
• World War II created pressure on Britain to gain Indian support.
• Growing nationalist demand for independence.
• Failure of earlier constitutional negotiations (Round Table Conferences).

PYQ Trap
• Cripps Mission directly linked with World War II context.

Leader of Mission

Important Personality
• Sir Stafford Cripps.

Proposals

Constitutional Proposals
• Dominion Status to be granted after the war.
• Creation of a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution.

Provincial Provision
• Provinces given the option to opt out of the Indian Union.

Safeguards
• British control over defence during the war.

PYQ Trap
• Right of provinces to secede → major controversial clause.

Reaction of Indian Leaders

Congress
• Rejected the proposal.

Reasons
• Dominion Status offered only after war (not immediate).
• Provision for provincial secession threatened unity.
• No real transfer of power during war.

Gandhi’s View
• Described it as “a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.”

Muslim League
• Also rejected as it did not fully satisfy demand for Pakistan.

PYQ Trap
• Both Congress and Muslim League rejected Cripps proposals.

Failure of Mission

Important Points
• Lack of immediate transfer of power.
• Distrust between British and Indian leaders.
• Controversial provisions on provincial autonomy.

Consequences

Political Impact
• Failure led to further distrust.
• Strengthened demand for complete independence.

Strategic Impact
• Directly led to the launch of Quit India Movement (1942).

PYQ Trap
• Cripps failure → Quit India Movement.

Significance

Important Points
• First official mention of Constituent Assembly.
• Recognized right of Indians to frame Constitution.

Comparative Analysis

Important Points
• Cripps Mission → Dominion Status after war.
• Lahore Session → Purna Swaraj (complete independence).

Conclusion
• The Cripps Mission failed to satisfy Indian aspirations.
• Its rejection intensified the freedom struggle and paved the way for the Quit India Movement.
Modern History.Quit India Movement (1942):
QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT (1942)

Introduction
• The Quit India Movement was the final mass movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi against British rule.
• It was initiated in August 1942 demanding immediate independence.
• It marked the peak of the Indian National Movement during World War II.

Background
• Failure of Cripps Mission (1942).
• Growing frustration with British unwillingness to transfer power.
• Impact of World War II on India.

PYQ Trap
• Quit India directly linked with failure of Cripps Mission.

Launch of Movement

Event
• All India Congress Committee session held at Bombay (August 1942).

Resolution
• Quit India Resolution passed.

Slogan
• “Do or Die.”

PYQ Trap
• Do or Die → Gandhi → Quit India Movement.

Leadership

Important Personalities
• Mahatma Gandhi
• Jawaharlal Nehru
• Sardar Patel

Immediate British Response

Important Points
• Arrest of all major leaders immediately after launch.
• Congress declared illegal.

PYQ Trap
• Movement became leaderless due to immediate arrests.

Nature of Movement

Features
• Mass uprising across India.
• Participation of students, workers and peasants.
• Spread of underground activities.

Underground Leadership

Important Personalities
• Jayaprakash Narayan
• Ram Manohar Lohia
• Aruna Asaf Ali

PYQ Trap
• Aruna Asaf Ali → hoisted flag during Quit India Movement.

Parallel Governments

Important Points
• Satara (Prati Sarkar) – Maharashtra.
• Ballia – Uttar Pradesh.
• Tamluk – Bengal.

PYQ Trap
• Parallel governments = key feature of Quit India.

Methods

Features
• Strikes and protests.
• Sabotage of communication lines.
• Refusal to cooperate with authorities.

Government Repression

Important Points
• Severe use of force.
• Mass arrests.
• Use of military power.

PYQ Trap
• Most violent suppression compared to earlier movements.

Significance

Political Impact
• Demonstrated strong nationalist sentiment.
• Made British realize urgency of transfer of power.

Strategic Impact
• Marked beginning of end of British rule in India.

Limitations

Important Points
• Lack of centralized leadership.
• Spontaneous and uncoordinated actions.

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Important Points
• NCM → withdrawn due to violence.
• CDM → structured phases.
• Quit India → spontaneous mass uprising.

PYQ Trap
• Quit India = most spontaneous and leaderless movement.

Conclusion
• The Quit India Movement was the final mass uprising against British rule.
• It played a decisive role in hastening India’s independence in 1947.
Modern History.Azad Hind Fauj / Indian National Army (I:
AZAD HIND FAUJ (INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY - INA)

Introduction
• The Indian National Army (INA), also known as Azad Hind Fauj, was formed to fight against British rule with the support of Axis powers during World War II.
• It represented the militant international phase of the Indian freedom struggle.

Background
• Large number of Indian soldiers were captured by Japanese forces in Southeast Asia during World War II.
• These prisoners were encouraged to join the struggle against British rule.

Formation

First Phase
• Initially formed in 1942 under Mohan Singh.
• Supported by Rash Behari Bose.

Second Phase (Reorganization)
• Revived and reorganized by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943.

PYQ Trap
• INA reorganized and led effectively by Subhas Chandra Bose.

Leadership

Important Personalities
• Subhas Chandra Bose (Netaji)
• Rash Behari Bose

Slogans
• “Give me blood, and I will give you freedom.”
• “Jai Hind.”

PYQ Trap
• Netaji associated with INA slogans.

Azad Hind Government (1943)

Introduction
• Provisional Government of Free India established in Singapore.

Features
• Declared war against British.
• Received recognition from Axis powers.

PYQ Trap
• Azad Hind Government → Singapore, 1943.

Military Campaigns

Important Points
• INA advanced towards India through Burma.
• Participated in battles of Imphal and Kohima.

Outcome
• Defeated due to Allied counter-offensive.

PYQ Trap
• INA linked with Imphal and Kohima campaigns.

Role of Women

Important Points
• Rani Jhansi Regiment formed.
• Led by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

PYQ Trap
• First all-women combat unit in Indian freedom struggle.

INA Trials (1945–46)

Introduction
• Trials held at Red Fort.

Impact
• Massive public support across India.
• Unified political groups against British.

Important Personalities
• Shah Nawaz Khan
• Prem Kumar Sehgal
• Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon

PYQ Trap
• INA trials triggered nationwide protests.

Significance

Political Impact
• Boosted nationalist sentiment.
• Inspired Indian armed forces.

Strategic Impact
• Contributed to decline of British authority.

Psychological Impact
• Demonstrated possibility of armed resistance.

Limitations

Important Points
• Dependent on Japanese support.
• Limited military success.

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Important Points
• Gandhian movement → non-violent.
• INA → armed struggle.

Conclusion
• The INA played a crucial role in intensifying the freedom struggle.
• Though militarily unsuccessful, it had a profound impact on weakening British control and accelerating independence.
Modern History.Cabinet Mission Plan (1946):
CABINET MISSION PLAN (1946)

Introduction
• The Cabinet Mission Plan was sent by the British Government in 1946 to devise a constitutional framework for India and facilitate transfer of power.
• It aimed to resolve the deadlock between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

Background
• Failure of Cripps Mission (1942).
• Rise of demand for Pakistan by Muslim League.
• Increasing pressure on Britain after World War II.

PYQ Trap
• Cabinet Mission = last major British attempt to keep India united.

Members of Mission

Important Personalities
• Lord Pethick-Lawrence
• Sir Stafford Cripps
• A.V. Alexander

PYQ Trap
• Cripps again part of Cabinet Mission.

Objectives

Important Points
• Transfer power to Indian hands.
• Maintain unity of India.
• Frame a constitution acceptable to all parties.

Main Proposals

Union Government
• A weak centre controlling only defence, foreign affairs and communications.

Provincial Autonomy
• Provinces given significant powers.

Grouping of Provinces
• Provinces grouped into three sections:
  Group A – Hindu-majority provinces
  Group B – Muslim-majority provinces (North-West)
  Group C – Muslim-majority provinces (East)

PYQ Trap
• Grouping plan is core feature of Cabinet Mission.

Constituent Assembly

Important Points
• Formation of Constituent Assembly to draft Constitution.
• Indirect election by provincial legislatures.

PYQ Trap
• Cabinet Mission → Constituent Assembly creation.

Interim Government

Important Points
• Formation of interim government at centre.

Reaction of Parties

Congress
• Accepted plan with reservations.
• Opposed compulsory grouping.

Muslim League
• Initially accepted.
• Later rejected and demanded Pakistan.

PYQ Trap
• Muslim League first accepted, then rejected Cabinet Mission Plan.

Failure of Plan

Important Points
• Disagreement over grouping of provinces.
• Conflict between Congress and Muslim League.
• League’s demand for Pakistan intensified.

Consequences

Political Impact
• Direct Action Day (1946) by Muslim League.
• Communal violence increased.

Strategic Impact
• Led to acceptance of Partition.

PYQ Trap
• Failure → Direct Action Day → Partition.

Significance

Important Points
• Proposed united India without partition.
• Provided basis for Constituent Assembly.

Comparative Analysis

Important Points
• Cripps Mission → Dominion status after war.
• Cabinet Mission → Constitution-making framework.

Conclusion
• The Cabinet Mission Plan was the last serious effort to preserve Indian unity.
• Its failure led directly to partition and independence in 1947.
Modern History.Mountbatten Plan (1947):
MOUNTBATTEN PLAN (1947)

Introduction
• The Mountbatten Plan, announced on 3 June 1947, provided the final framework for the transfer of power from British rule to Indian hands.
• It accepted the demand for partition of India.

Background
• Failure of Cabinet Mission Plan (1946).
• Escalation of communal violence after Direct Action Day (1946).
• Inability of Congress and Muslim League to reach agreement.

PYQ Trap
• Mountbatten Plan directly linked with Partition decision.

Key Personality

Important Personality
• Lord Louis Mountbatten (last Viceroy of India).

Main Provisions

Partition of India
• British India to be divided into two dominions – India and Pakistan.

Princely States
• Given option to join either India or Pakistan.

Punjab and Bengal
• Partition of provinces through Boundary Commissions.

Referendum
• NWFP and Sylhet to decide their future through referendum.

Transfer of Power
• Independence to be granted in August 1947.

PYQ Trap
• Boundary Commission → Radcliffe Commission.

Radcliffe Commission

Introduction
• Set up to demarcate boundaries between India and Pakistan.

Features
• Headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.

PYQ Trap
• Radcliffe Line → India-Pakistan boundary.

Acceptance of Plan

Congress
• Accepted as practical solution to avoid civil war.

Muslim League
• Accepted as it fulfilled demand for Pakistan.

PYQ Trap
• Both Congress and League accepted Mountbatten Plan.

Consequences

Partition
• Division of India into India and Pakistan.

Violence
• Massive communal riots and migration.

Strategic Impact
• End of British rule.

Significance

Political Impact
• Final decision leading to independence.

Administrative Impact
• Framework for Indian Independence Act, 1947.

Limitations

Important Points
• Hasty implementation.
• Inadequate preparation for partition.

Comparative Analysis

Important Points
• Cabinet Mission Plan → attempted unity.
• Mountbatten Plan → accepted partition.

PYQ Trap
• CMP = united India, MBP = partition.

Conclusion
• The Mountbatten Plan marked the end of British efforts to keep India united.
• It paved the way for independence but also led to the traumatic partition of the subcontinent.
Modern History.Indian Independence Act (1947):
INDIAN INDEPENDENCE ACT, 1947

Introduction
• The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was passed by the British Parliament to transfer power to Indian hands.
• It provided the legal basis for the creation of two independent dominions – India and Pakistan.

Background
• Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947).
• Failure of earlier constitutional attempts to maintain unity.
• Increasing communal tensions and demand for partition.

PYQ Trap
• Independence Act based on Mountbatten Plan.

Key Features

Creation of Dominions
• India and Pakistan became independent dominions on 15 August 1947.

End of British Authority
• British Parliament ceased to have authority over India.

Governor-General
• Each dominion to have its own Governor-General.

Constituent Assemblies
• Given power to frame their own constitutions.

PYQ Trap
• Constituent Assembly gained full sovereignty after Act.

Legislative Sovereignty

Important Points
• Laws of British Parliament no longer applicable.
• Indian legislature became sovereign.

Abolition of Secretary of State
• Office of Secretary of State for India abolished.

Princely States

Important Points
• British suzerainty over princely states ended.
• States free to join India or Pakistan.

PYQ Trap
• Suzerainty ended → not automatically integrated.

Partition Provisions

Important Points
• Division of British India into India and Pakistan.
• Boundary demarcation by Radcliffe Commission.

Civil Services and Armed Forces

Important Points
• Division between India and Pakistan.

Significance

Political Impact
• Legal end of British rule.
• Establishment of independent governance.

Administrative Impact
• Framework for functioning of new states.

Strategic Impact
• Enabled constitution-making process.

Limitations

Important Points
• Led to partition and communal violence.
• Immediate administrative challenges.

Comparative Analysis

Important Points
• Mountbatten Plan → political framework.
• Independence Act → legal implementation.

PYQ Trap
• Plan vs Act distinction is frequently tested.

Conclusion
• The Indian Independence Act marked the formal end of British colonial rule in India.
• It paved the way for independent governance and constitution-making in both India and Pakistan.

Polity.Historical Background of Indian Constitu:
HISTORICAL BACKGROUND OF INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Indian Constitution is the result of a long historical evolution under British rule.
• Various Acts passed by the British Parliament gradually shaped the administrative, legislative and constitutional framework of India.

Important Points
• Evolution was gradual from Company rule to Crown rule.
• Each Act introduced new administrative and constitutional features.

PYQ Trap
• Questions are often asked on features introduced by specific Acts.

REGULATING ACT OF 1773

Features
• First step towards parliamentary control over East India Company.
• Governor of Bengal became Governor-General of Bengal.
• Established Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774).

PYQ Trap
• First Governor-General → Warren Hastings.

PITTS INDIA ACT 1784

Features
• Introduced dual system of control.
• Board of Control established to supervise Company.

PYQ Trap
• Dual control → Company + British Government.

CHARTER ACT 1813

Features
• Ended Company’s trade monopoly except tea and China trade.
• Allowed Christian missionaries.

CHARTER ACT 1833

Features
• Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India.
• Centralized administration.
• Law Commission established.

PYQ Trap
• First Governor-General of India → Lord William Bentinck.

CHARTER ACT 1853

Features
• Introduced open competition for civil services.
• Separated legislative and executive functions.

PYQ Trap
• First time legislative-executive separation introduced.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1858

Features
• Ended Company rule.
• Power transferred to British Crown.
• Secretary of State for India created.

PYQ Trap
• Beginning of Crown rule in India.

INDIAN COUNCILS ACT 1861

Features
• Introduced legislative councils.
• Allowed Indians to be nominated.

PYQ Trap
• First step towards association of Indians in legislation.

INDIAN COUNCILS ACT 1892

Features
• Introduced indirect elections.
• Increased representation of Indians.

INDIAN COUNCILS ACT 1909 (MORLEY-MINTO REFORMS)

Features
• Introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
• Increased Indian participation.

PYQ Trap
• First introduction of communal representation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1919 (MONTAGU-CHELMSFORD REFORMS)

Features
• Introduced dyarchy in provinces.
• Bicameral legislature at centre.

PYQ Trap
• Dyarchy = division of subjects into transferred and reserved.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1935

Features
• Proposed federal structure.
• Introduced provincial autonomy.
• Bicameralism in some provinces.

PYQ Trap
• Largest Act and major source of Indian Constitution.

INDIAN INDEPENDENCE ACT 1947

Features
• Partition of India into India and Pakistan.
• End of British rule.
• Constituent Assembly given full powers.

PYQ Trap
• Legal basis of independence.

Significance
• Provided administrative and constitutional framework.
• Many provisions adopted in Indian Constitution.

Conclusion
• The historical background reflects gradual evolution of constitutional governance in India.
• It laid the foundation for the making of the Indian Constitution.
Polity.Making of the Constitution:
MAKING OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly between 1946 and 1949.
• It represents the will of the people and is the longest written Constitution in the world.

Causes
• Demand for self-governance during freedom struggle.
• Failure of British constitutional experiments.
• Need for a democratic framework after independence.

PYQ Trap
• Constitution framed by Constituent Assembly, not British Parliament.

CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY

Features
• Formed in 1946 under Cabinet Mission Plan.
• Members indirectly elected by provincial assemblies.
• Total strength initially 389.

Important Points
• After partition → strength reduced to 299.
• First meeting held on 9 December 1946.

PYQ Trap
• First meeting presided by Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (temporary president).

Leadership
• Dr. Rajendra Prasad → President of Constituent Assembly.
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar → Chairman of Drafting Committee.

PYQ Trap
• Ambedkar = Chairman of Drafting Committee (very important).

COMMITTEES OF CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY

Important Points
• Drafting Committee – B.R. Ambedkar
• Union Constitution Committee – Jawaharlal Nehru
• Fundamental Rights Committee – Sardar Patel

PYQ Trap
• Patel handled Fundamental Rights and Minorities committees.

DRAFTING OF CONSTITUTION

Features
• Drafting Committee formed in 1947.
• Draft Constitution prepared by B.N. Rau (Constitutional Advisor).

Important Points
• Final draft adopted on 26 November 1949.
• Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

PYQ Trap
• 26 November → Adoption, 26 January → Enforcement.

TIME TAKEN

Important Points
• Took 2 years, 11 months, 18 days.

COST OF CONSTITUTION

Important Points
• Approx. ₹64 lakh spent.

SOURCES OF CONSTITUTION

Features
• Borrowed from multiple countries.

Important Points
• UK → Parliamentary system
• USA → Fundamental Rights
• Ireland → DPSP
• Canada → Federal system with strong centre

PYQ Trap
• Borrowed features frequently asked.

SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS OF ASSEMBLY

Important Points
• Representative body.
• Included leaders from different backgrounds.
• Debates ensured detailed discussion.

CRITICISM

Important Points
• Not directly elected by people.
• Dominated by Congress.

Significance
• Provided democratic foundation.
• Reflected diversity of India.
• Ensured rights and governance structure.

Conclusion
• The Constituent Assembly successfully framed a comprehensive Constitution.
• It laid the foundation for democratic governance in independent India.
Polity.Salient Features of the Indian Constitut:
SALIENT FEATURES OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Indian Constitution is a unique document combining features from various constitutions of the world.
• It establishes a sovereign, democratic framework for governance.

Important Points
• Longest written Constitution in the world.
• Blend of rigidity and flexibility.

PYQ Trap
• Indian Constitution is neither fully rigid nor fully flexible.

WRITTEN AND DETAILED CONSTITUTION

Features
• Contains detailed provisions regarding governance.
• Originally had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules.

PYQ Trap
• Presently → 450+ Articles and 12 Schedules.

SOVEREIGN STATE

Features
• India is independent in internal and external matters.

SOCIALIST AND SECULAR STATE

Features
• Added by 42nd Amendment (1976).
• Ensures equality and religious neutrality.

PYQ Trap
• Socialist and Secular added later, not original.

DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC

Features
• Government elected by people.
• President is elected (not hereditary).

PARLIAMENTARY SYSTEM

Features
• Executive responsible to legislature.
• Prime Minister is real executive.

PYQ Trap
• Parliamentary system borrowed from UK.

FEDERAL SYSTEM WITH UNITARY BIAS

Features
• Division of powers between Centre and States.
• Strong central government.

PYQ Trap
• India is federal but with unitary features.

INTEGRATED JUDICIARY

Features
• Single unified judicial system.
• Supreme Court at top.

FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Guarantee civil liberties.
• Justiciable in courts.

PYQ Trap
• Enforceable by courts (key point).

DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY

Features
• Guidelines for state policy.
• Non-justiciable.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP not enforceable in courts.

FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Features
• Added by 42nd Amendment.

UNIVERSAL ADULT FRANCHISE

Features
• All citizens above 18 years can vote.

PYQ Trap
• Voting age reduced from 21 to 18 by 61st Amendment.

INDEPENDENT JUDICIARY

Features
• Judiciary free from executive interference.

EMERGENCY PROVISIONS

Features
• Centre gets more power during emergencies.

PYQ Trap
• Emergency provisions borrowed from Germany.

SINGLE CITIZENSHIP

Features
• Only one citizenship for entire country.

PYQ Trap
• Unlike USA, India has single citizenship.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures stability and flexibility.
• Maintains unity in diversity.
• Protects rights and governance structure.

Conclusion
• The Indian Constitution is a balanced document combining global ideas with Indian needs.
• It forms the backbone of democratic governance in India.
Polity.Preamble:
PREAMBLE OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

Introduction
• The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution which sets out the philosophy and objectives of the Constitution.
• It reflects the ideals and aspirations of the people of India.

Important Points
• Based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946.

PYQ Trap
• Preamble is based on Objectives Resolution.

KEY WORDS IN PREAMBLE

Features
• Sovereign – India is independent internally and externally.
• Socialist – Promotes social and economic equality.
• Secular – Equal respect to all religions.
• Democratic – Government elected by people.
• Republic – Head of state is elected.

PYQ Trap
• Socialist and Secular added by 42nd Amendment (1976).

OBJECTIVES OF PREAMBLE

Features
• Justice – Social, Economic and Political.
• Liberty – Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.
• Equality – Status and opportunity.
• Fraternity – Unity and integrity of the nation.

PYQ Trap
• Fraternity ensures dignity of individual and unity of nation.

NATURE OF PREAMBLE

Important Points
• Not a source of power.
• Acts as guiding principle for interpretation.

PYQ Trap
• Preamble is not enforceable in court.

AMENDABILITY OF PREAMBLE

Important Points
• Preamble can be amended under Article 368.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda Bharati case → Preamble is part of Constitution.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Reflects core philosophy of Constitution.
• Helps in interpretation of constitutional provisions.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Berubari Case (1960) → Preamble not part of Constitution (initial view).
• Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973) → Preamble is part of Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• Kesavananda reversed Berubari.

CONCLUSION

Conclusion
• The Preamble is the soul of the Constitution.
• It guides the functioning of the Indian political system.
Polity.Citizenship:
CITIZENSHIP

Introduction
• Citizenship denotes the legal relationship between an individual and the State.
• It provides rights, duties and political identity to a person.

Important Points
• Articles 5 to 11 deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• Citizenship provisions in Constitution are temporary in nature.

CONSTITUTIONAL PROVISIONS

Features
• Article 5 – Citizenship at commencement.
• Article 6 – Citizenship for migrants from Pakistan.
• Article 7 – Citizenship for migrants to Pakistan.
• Article 8 – Citizenship for persons of Indian origin abroad.
• Article 9 – No dual citizenship.
• Article 10 – Continuance of citizenship.
• Article 11 – Parliament’s power to regulate citizenship.

PYQ Trap
• Parliament has power to regulate citizenship under Article 11.

CITIZENSHIP ACT 1955

Features
• Provides detailed provisions for acquisition and loss of citizenship.

MODES OF ACQUIRING CITIZENSHIP

Features
• By Birth
• By Descent
• By Registration
• By Naturalization
• By Incorporation of Territory

PYQ Trap
• Incorporation of territory is rarely asked but important.

LOSS OF CITIZENSHIP

Features
• By Renunciation
• By Termination
• By Deprivation

PYQ Trap
• Deprivation applies in cases of fraud or disloyalty.

SINGLE CITIZENSHIP

Features
• India follows single citizenship for entire country.

PYQ Trap
• Unlike USA → no dual citizenship in India.

OVERSEAS CITIZENSHIP OF INDIA (OCI)

Features
• Introduced by amendment to Citizenship Act.
• Provides multiple entry, lifelong visa.

Important Points
• OCI is not dual citizenship.

PYQ Trap
• OCI holders do not have voting rights.

RIGHTS AVAILABLE TO CITIZENS ONLY

Features
• Article 15 – Prohibition of discrimination.
• Article 16 – Equality in public employment.
• Article 19 – Freedom rights.

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 available only to citizens.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Defines membership of State.
• Ensures political participation.

Conclusion
• Citizenship is fundamental to the functioning of a democratic State.
• It defines the rights and responsibilities of individuals in India.
Polity.Fundamental Rights:
FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Introduction
• Fundamental Rights (FRs) are the cornerstone of political democracy in India.
• They guarantee civil liberties and act as limitations on State power.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part III (Articles 12–35).
• Inspired largely from the Bill of Rights (USA).

PYQ Trap
• Part III = Fundamental Rights (very frequent question).

FEATURES OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Justiciable and enforceable by courts.
• Available against State action (Article 12 defines State).
• Some rights available only to citizens, others to all persons.
• Not absolute – subject to reasonable restrictions.

PYQ Trap
• Article 12 includes Government, Parliament, State Legislature and authorities.

CLASSIFICATION OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)
• Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30)
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32)

PYQ Trap
• Right to Property removed from FR by 44th Amendment (1978).

RIGHT TO EQUALITY

Features
• Article 14 → Equality before law + equal protection of laws.
• Article 15 → Prohibition of discrimination.
• Article 16 → Equality in public employment.
• Article 17 → Abolition of untouchability.
• Article 18 → Abolition of titles.

PYQ Trap
• Article 17 is absolute (no exceptions).

RIGHT TO FREEDOM

Features
• Article 19 → Six freedoms (speech, assembly, association, movement, residence, profession).
• Article 20 → Protection in criminal laws.
• Article 21 → Right to life and personal liberty.
• Article 22 → Protection against arbitrary arrest.

Important Points
• Article 21 expanded through judicial interpretation (Right to privacy, livelihood, dignity).

PYQ Trap
• Article 21 = most dynamic and expansive right.

RIGHT AGAINST EXPLOITATION

Features
• Article 23 → Prohibits trafficking and forced labour.
• Article 24 → Prohibits child labour in hazardous industries.

RIGHT TO FREEDOM OF RELIGION

Features
• Article 25 → Freedom of conscience and religion.
• Article 26 → Manage religious affairs.
• Article 27 → No tax for promotion of religion.
• Article 28 → No religious instruction in State institutions.

PYQ Trap
• Subject to public order, morality and health.

CULTURAL AND EDUCATIONAL RIGHTS

Features
• Article 29 → Protection of culture and language.
• Article 30 → Minority institutions rights.

PYQ Trap
• Applies to minorities (religious and linguistic).

RIGHT TO CONSTITUTIONAL REMEDIES

Features
• Article 32 → Right to approach Supreme Court.
• Provides remedies for enforcement of FRs.

Important Points
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution”.

WRITS

Features
• Habeas Corpus – produce detained person.
• Mandamus – command public authority.
• Prohibition – stop lower court.
• Certiorari – quash lower court order.
• Quo Warranto – question authority.

PYQ Trap
• Habeas Corpus most frequently asked.

RESTRICTIONS ON FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• Reasonable restrictions imposed by State.
• Grounds include security, public order, morality, etc.

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 rights are not absolute.

SUSPENSION OF FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS

Features
• During National Emergency (Article 352).

Important Points
• Article 20 and 21 cannot be suspended (44th Amendment).

PYQ Trap
• Article 19 automatically suspended only during war/emergency.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Golaknath Case (1967) → FR cannot be amended (initial view).
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Basic Structure doctrine.
• Maneka Gandhi Case (1978) → Expanded Article 21.

PYQ Trap
• Maneka Gandhi case = due process expansion.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures individual liberty.
• Protects against arbitrary State action.
• Strengthens rule of law.

Conclusion
• Fundamental Rights are essential for maintaining democracy and individual dignity.
• They form the backbone of the Indian constitutional framework.
Polity.Directive Principles of State Policy:
DIRECTIVE PRINCIPLES OF STATE POLICY

Introduction
• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are constitutional directives to the State for establishing social and economic democracy.
• They aim to transform India into a welfare state.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36–51).
• Inspired from Irish Constitution.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP borrowed from Ireland.

FEATURES OF DPSP

Features
• Non-justiciable – cannot be enforced by courts.
• Fundamental in governance of the country (Article 37).
• Binding on State morally, not legally.

PYQ Trap
• Article 37 → DPSP not enforceable but fundamental in governance.

CLASSIFICATION OF DPSP

Features
• Socialist Principles
• Gandhian Principles
• Liberal-Intellectual Principles

PYQ Trap
• Classification is not mentioned in Constitution.

SOCIALIST PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 38 → Promote welfare of people.
• Article 39 → Equal distribution of resources, equal pay.
• Article 41 → Right to work, education and public assistance.
• Article 42 → Just and humane conditions of work.
• Article 43 → Living wage.

PYQ Trap
• Article 39(d) → Equal pay for equal work.

GANDHIAN PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 40 → Organisation of village panchayats.
• Article 43 → Promotion of cottage industries.
• Article 46 → Promotion of SC/ST welfare.

PYQ Trap
• Panchayati Raj rooted in Article 40.

LIBERAL-INTELLECTUAL PRINCIPLES

Features
• Article 44 → Uniform Civil Code.
• Article 45 → Early childhood care and education.
• Article 48A → Protection of environment.
• Article 50 → Separation of judiciary from executive.

PYQ Trap
• Article 48A added by 42nd Amendment.

RELATION BETWEEN FR AND DPSP

Important Points
• FR → enforceable rights.
• DPSP → non-enforceable goals.
• Both are complementary, not contradictory.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Champakam Dorairajan (1951) → FR prevail over DPSP.
• Golaknath (1967) → Limited Parliament power over FR.
• Kesavananda Bharati (1973) → Harmony between FR and DPSP.
• Minerva Mills (1980) → Balance between FR and DPSP is part of basic structure.

PYQ Trap
• Minerva Mills → balance between FR and DPSP.

IMPLEMENTATION OF DPSP

Features
• Land reforms and abolition of zamindari.
• Panchayati Raj institutions.
• MGNREGA reflects Article 41.

PYQ Trap
• DPSP implemented through laws, not directly enforceable.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Promote social and economic justice.
• Guide policymaking.
• Reduce inequalities.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• No legal enforcement.
• Depend on political will.

Conclusion
• DPSP provide the blueprint for a welfare state.
• They complement Fundamental Rights in achieving constitutional goals.
Polity.Fundamental Duties:
FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Introduction
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations imposed on citizens to promote national discipline, unity and integrity.
• They complement Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

Important Points
• Enshrined in Part IVA (Article 51A).
• Added by 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

PYQ Trap
• Fundamental Duties added during Emergency period (1976).

FEATURES OF FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

Features
• Non-justiciable – not enforceable by courts.
• Apply only to citizens (not to foreigners).
• Derived from the Constitution of USSR (Soviet Union).

PYQ Trap
• Duties apply only to citizens (important elimination point).

NUMBER OF DUTIES

Important Points
• Originally 10 duties.
• 11th duty added by 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

PYQ Trap
• 11th duty relates to education of children between 6–14 years.

LIST OF IMPORTANT DUTIES

Features
• Respect Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem.
• Promote harmony and spirit of brotherhood.
• Preserve rich heritage of culture.
• Protect environment (forests, lakes, wildlife).
• Safeguard public property.
• Develop scientific temper.

PYQ Trap
• Environmental protection duty frequently asked in prelims.

NATURE OF DUTIES

Important Points
• Not legally enforceable, but can be enforced through laws.
• Courts can consider them while interpreting laws.

PYQ Trap
• Duties indirectly enforceable through legislation.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Courts have used Fundamental Duties to interpret constitutional validity of laws.
• Environmental judgments often refer to Article 51A(g).

PYQ Trap
• Article 51A(g) → environment protection.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Promote civic responsibility and patriotism.
• Help in maintaining discipline and national unity.
• Strengthen democratic structure.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• No direct enforcement mechanism.
• Some duties are vague and open-ended.

Conclusion
• Fundamental Duties serve as ethical obligations for citizens.
• They balance rights with responsibilities in a democratic system.
Polity.President of India:
PRESIDENT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The President is the constitutional head of the State and the first citizen of India.
• All executive actions are taken in the name of the President.

Important Points
• Articles 52–78 deal with Union Executive.

PYQ Trap
• President is nominal executive, real power with Council of Ministers.

ELECTION OF PRESIDENT

Features
• Elected indirectly by Electoral College.

Important Points
• Electoral College includes:
  – Elected members of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
  – Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
• Nominated members are not included.

PYQ Trap
• MLAs of Union Territories (Delhi & Puducherry) also participate.

ELECTION METHOD

Features
• Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote.
• Secret ballot.

PYQ Trap
• Value of vote differs for MPs and MLAs.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.
• Qualified for Lok Sabha membership.

TENURE

Features
• 5 years term.
• Eligible for re-election.

REMOVAL (IMPEACHMENT)

Features
• Can be removed for violation of Constitution.

Important Points
• Impeachment initiated by either House of Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• Impeachment is quasi-judicial in nature.

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Appoints Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.
• Appoints Governors, Judges, CAG, Election Commissioners.

PYQ Trap
• Appointments are made on advice of Council of Ministers.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Summons and prorogues Parliament.
• Addresses Parliament.
• Assent to bills.

Important Points
• Can return ordinary bill for reconsideration.

PYQ Trap
• Cannot return Money Bill.

ORDINANCE POWER

Features
• Article 123 → Can promulgate ordinance when Parliament not in session.

PYQ Trap
• Ordinance has same force as law.

JUDICIAL POWERS

Features
• Article 72 → Power to grant pardon, reprieve, respite, remission, commutation.

PYQ Trap
• President can pardon death sentence.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Money Bill can be introduced only with President’s recommendation.
• Annual Budget presented in name of President.

EMERGENCY POWERS

Features
• National Emergency (Article 352)
• State Emergency (Article 356)
• Financial Emergency (Article 360)

PYQ Trap
• President acts on advice of Cabinet in emergency.

VETO POWERS

Features
• Absolute veto → Reject bill.
• Suspensive veto → Return bill.
• Pocket veto → No action.

PYQ Trap
• Pocket veto used in India (e.g., Zail Singh case).

DISCRETIONARY POWERS

Important Points
• Limited discretionary powers.
• Mainly in appointment of PM when no clear majority.

PYQ Trap
• President usually bound by advice of Council of Ministers (Article 74).

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• 42nd Amendment → Made advice binding.
• 44th Amendment → President can ask reconsideration once.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures continuity of government.
• Symbol of unity and integrity of nation.

Conclusion
• The President is the nominal executive with vast constitutional powers.
• Functions largely on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.
Polity.Vice President:
VICE-PRESIDENT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The Vice-President is the second highest constitutional office in India.
• He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Articles 63–71 deal with Vice-President.

PYQ Trap
• Vice-President is not part of executive like President.

ELECTION OF VICE-PRESIDENT

Features
• Elected indirectly.

Important Points
• Electoral College includes:
  – Members of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated)

PYQ Trap
• Unlike President, nominated members also vote.

ELECTION METHOD

Features
• Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote.
• Secret ballot.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.
• Qualified for Rajya Sabha membership.

PYQ Trap
• Qualification linked to Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha.

TENURE

Features
• Term of 5 years.

Important Points
• Eligible for re-election.

REMOVAL

Features
• Removed by resolution of Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Requires majority in Rajya Sabha and agreement of Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• No formal impeachment like President.

FUNCTIONS OF VICE-PRESIDENT

LEGISLATIVE ROLE

Features
• Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Presides over proceedings of Rajya Sabha.
• Maintains order and discipline.

PYQ Trap
• Does not vote in first instance, only casting vote in case of tie.

EXECUTIVE ROLE

Features
• Acts as President in absence of President.

Important Points
• Performs functions during vacancy or absence of President.

PYQ Trap
• Acts as President, not becomes President.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• Acts as substitute when President unable to discharge duties.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures continuity in executive.
• Maintains functioning of Rajya Sabha.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Limited executive powers.
• Mainly legislative role.

Conclusion
• The Vice-President plays a dual role as presiding officer of Rajya Sabha and as a standby executive authority.
• Though limited in powers, the office is crucial for constitutional continuity.
Polity.Prime Minister:
PRIME MINISTER

Introduction
• The Prime Minister is the real executive authority in India.
• He is the head of the Council of Ministers and the leader of the government.

Important Points
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Real executive = Prime Minister, not President.

APPOINTMENT OF PRIME MINISTER

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Leader of majority party in Lok Sabha is appointed.
• In case of no clear majority → President exercises discretion.

PYQ Trap
• PM must prove majority in Lok Sabha.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Must be a member of Parliament.

Important Points
• If not a member → must become MP within 6 months.

PYQ Trap
• PM can be from Rajya Sabha also.

POSITION AND ROLE

Features
• Head of government.
• Leader of Lok Sabha (usually).
• Principal advisor to President.

PYQ Trap
• PM is the pivot of entire political system.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Selects and appoints Council of Ministers.
• Allocates portfolios.
• Can recommend removal of ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Ministers hold office at pleasure of President but actually controlled by PM.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Leader of House.
• Decides government agenda in Parliament.
• Advises President on summoning and dissolution.

PYQ Trap
• PM plays key role in legislative process.

ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS

Features
• Coordinates work of ministries.
• Chairs Cabinet meetings.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Plays key role in budget formulation through Cabinet.

DIPLOMATIC POWERS

Features
• Represents India internationally.
• Shapes foreign policy.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• Acts as link between President and Council of Ministers.
• Advises President on all matters.

PYQ Trap
• President bound by advice of PM (Article 74).

COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Features
• Collective responsibility to Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Collective responsibility = core feature of parliamentary system.

TENURE OF PRIME MINISTER

Features
• No fixed tenure.
• Continues as long as majority support exists.

REMOVAL

Features
• Removed when loses majority in Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• No impeachment for PM.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Central figure in administration.
• Ensures stability and policy direction.

Conclusion
• The Prime Minister is the real centre of power in Indian polity.
• The entire governance system revolves around the office of the Prime Minister.
Polity.Council of Ministers:
COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Introduction
• The Council of Ministers (CoM) is the real executive body that exercises actual authority in India.
• It functions under the leadership of the Prime Minister.

Important Points
• Articles 74 and 75 deal with Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Real executive = Council of Ministers, not President.

COMPOSITION OF COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Features
• Cabinet Ministers
• Ministers of State (with or without independent charge)
• Deputy Ministers

PYQ Trap
• Constitution does not classify ministers into categories.

APPOINTMENT

Features
• Appointed by the President on advice of Prime Minister.

Important Points
• Prime Minister selects ministers.

PYQ Trap
• President has no independent choice in appointment.

COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY

Features
• Council of Ministers collectively responsible to Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• All ministers stand or fall together.

PYQ Trap
• Collective responsibility is core feature of parliamentary system.

INDIVIDUAL RESPONSIBILITY

Features
• Ministers hold office during pleasure of President.

Important Points
• In practice → controlled by Prime Minister.

PYQ Trap
• Pleasure of President = actually pleasure of PM.

TENURE

Features
• No fixed tenure.

Important Points
• Continues as long as majority in Lok Sabha exists.

LIMIT ON SIZE OF MINISTRY

Features
• 91st Amendment Act (2003).

Important Points
• Maximum size = 15% of Lok Sabha strength.

PYQ Trap
• Applies to both Union and State governments.

CABINET

Features
• Inner core of Council of Ministers.

Important Points
• Takes major policy decisions.

PYQ Trap
• Cabinet is not mentioned in original Constitution.

CABINET COMMITTEES

Features
• Smaller groups for efficient decision-making.

ROLE AND FUNCTIONS

EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS

Features
• Formulation and execution of policies.

LEGISLATIVE FUNCTIONS

Features
• Introduces bills and controls legislative agenda.

FINANCIAL FUNCTIONS

Features
• Prepares budget.

RELATION WITH PRESIDENT

Important Points
• President acts on advice of Council of Ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Advice binding after 42nd Amendment.

IMPORTANT AMENDMENTS

Important Points
• 42nd Amendment → Made advice binding.
• 44th Amendment → President can ask reconsideration once.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Core decision-making body.
• Ensures coordination in administration.

Conclusion
• The Council of Ministers is the real executive authority in India.
• It ensures effective governance under the parliamentary system.
Polity.Parliament:
PARLIAMENT

Introduction
• Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India.
• It consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Articles 79–122 deal with Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• President is an integral part of Parliament.

COMPOSITION OF PARLIAMENT

Features
• President
• Lok Sabha (House of People)
• Rajya Sabha (Council of States)

PYQ Trap
• Parliament ≠ only Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

LOK SABHA

Features
• Lower House, directly elected.

Important Points
• Maximum strength → 552.
• Present strength → 543 elected members.
• Tenure → 5 years (can be dissolved earlier).

PYQ Trap
• Only Lok Sabha can be dissolved.

RAJYA SABHA

Features
• Upper House, permanent body.

Important Points
• Maximum strength → 250.
• 1/3rd members retire every 2 years.
• Tenure of members → 6 years.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.

SPEAKER OF LOK SABHA

Features
• Presiding officer of Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Decides Money Bill status.
• Maintains order in House.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker’s decision on Money Bill is final.

LEGISLATIVE PROCEDURE

Features
• Bills can be introduced in either House.

Important Points
• Ordinary Bill → Both Houses must pass.
• Joint sitting possible in case of deadlock.

PYQ Trap
• Joint sitting only for Ordinary Bills.

MONEY BILL

Features
• Article 110 defines Money Bill.

Important Points
• Can be introduced only in Lok Sabha.
• Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha cannot reject Money Bill.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Budget presented annually.

Important Points
• Demand for grants voted only by Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha has no voting power on grants.

CONTROL OVER EXECUTIVE

Features
• Question Hour, Zero Hour.
• No-confidence motion.

PYQ Trap
• No-confidence motion only in Lok Sabha.

SPECIAL POWERS OF RAJYA SABHA

Features
• Article 249 → Can allow Parliament to legislate on State List.
• Article 312 → Creation of All India Services.

PYQ Trap
• Rajya Sabha has special federal powers.

PARLIAMENTARY PRIVILEGES

Features
• Freedom of speech in Parliament.
• Immunity from court proceedings.

PYQ Trap
• Privileges not fully codified.

IMPORTANT ARTICLES

Important Points
• Article 79 → Constitution of Parliament.
• Article 85 → Sessions of Parliament.
• Article 110 → Money Bill.
• Article 111 → Assent to Bills.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Law-making body of India.
• Controls executive.
• Represents people and states.

Conclusion
• Parliament is the cornerstone of Indian democracy.
• It ensures accountability, representation and law-making.
Polity.Parliamentary Devices:
PARLIAMENTARY DEVICES

Introduction
• Parliamentary devices are procedural instruments through which Members of Parliament control the executive, raise public issues and secure accountability.
• They are central to the functioning of parliamentary democracy in India.

Important Points
• These devices are mainly exercised inside Parliament, especially in Lok Sabha.
• They help in discussion, scrutiny and political accountability.

PYQ Trap
• Parliament controls the executive mainly through procedures, debates and motions, not merely through law-making.

QUESTION HOUR

Introduction
• Question Hour is the first hour of a sitting of Parliament in which members ask questions to ministers.

Features
• Ministers are bound to answer questions relating to their departments.
• It is one of the most effective instruments of parliamentary control.

Important Points
• Questions may be Starred, Unstarred or Short Notice.
• Starred Question requires oral answer and allows supplementary questions.
• Unstarred Question requires written answer and no supplementary question.

PYQ Trap
• Supplementary questions are allowed only in Starred Questions, not in Unstarred Questions.

ZERO HOUR

Introduction
• Zero Hour is an informal parliamentary device through which members raise urgent matters without prior listing in the formal agenda.

Features
• It starts immediately after Question Hour.
• It is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure.

Important Points
• It evolved through parliamentary practice in India.
• It reflects flexibility of Indian parliamentary functioning.

PYQ Trap
• Zero Hour is not a constitutional or rule-based device; it is a convention.

MOTION

Introduction
• A motion is a formal proposal moved by a member for discussion and decision of the House.

Features
• It allows the House to discuss a matter and express its opinion or will.

Important Points
• Motions may be substantive, substitute or subsidiary.

PYQ Trap
• Every resolution is a kind of motion, but not every motion becomes a resolution.

NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION

Introduction
• A No-Confidence Motion is moved in Lok Sabha to test whether the Council of Ministers enjoys majority support.

Features
• If passed, the Council of Ministers must resign.
• It can be moved only in Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Needs support of at least 50 members to be admitted.
• It reflects collective responsibility of Council of Ministers to Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• No-Confidence Motion is not available in Rajya Sabha because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible only to Lok Sabha.

CENSURE MOTION

Introduction
• A Censure Motion is moved to criticize specific policies or actions of the government.

Features
• It must state reasons or charges.
• It may not necessarily lead to resignation of the government.

PYQ Trap
• Unlike No-Confidence Motion, Censure Motion must mention specific grounds.

ADJOURNMENT MOTION

Introduction
• Adjournment Motion is an extraordinary device to draw attention to a definite matter of urgent public importance.

Features
• It interrupts normal business of the House.
• It is regarded as a strong form of censure against the government.

Important Points
• It is allowed only in Lok Sabha.
• The matter must be definite, urgent and of public importance.

PYQ Trap
• Adjournment Motion is an exceptional device and is not available in Rajya Sabha.

CALLING ATTENTION MOTION

Introduction
• Calling Attention is a device through which a member calls the attention of a minister to an urgent matter of public importance.

Features
• The minister makes a brief statement and members may seek clarifications.

Important Points
• It is an Indian innovation in parliamentary procedure.

PYQ Trap
• Calling Attention is different from Adjournment Motion because it does not interrupt business in the same disruptive manner.

SHORT DURATION DISCUSSION

Introduction
• Short Duration Discussion allows members to discuss a matter of urgent public importance without a formal motion.

Features
• No formal voting takes place.
• It is meant for discussion rather than decision.

PYQ Trap
• Short Duration Discussion ends without voting.

HALF-AN-HOUR DISCUSSION

Introduction
• Half-an-Hour Discussion is used to discuss matters arising out of answers given during Question Hour that require further clarification.

Features
• It is limited in duration and scope.

PYQ Trap
• It arises out of questions already answered in the House.

RESOLUTION

Introduction
• A resolution is a formal expression of opinion, recommendation or decision of the House.

Features
• It may be moved by ministers or private members.

Important Points
• Private Member’s Resolution is moved by a member who is not a minister.

PYQ Trap
• Resolutions are more formal than ordinary discussions and may express the final sense of the House.

POINT OF ORDER

Introduction
• A Point of Order is raised when a member feels that proceedings of the House are not being conducted according to rules.

Features
• It relates strictly to interpretation or enforcement of rules.

PYQ Trap
• A Point of Order does not permit general discussion on the issue.

PRIVILEGE MOTION

Introduction
• Privilege Motion is moved when a member believes that a minister or another member has breached parliamentary privilege.

Features
• It protects the dignity and authority of Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• It is linked with breach of privilege, not merely disagreement with a statement.

CUT MOTIONS

Introduction
• Cut Motions are moved during discussion on Demands for Grants to reduce the amount of demand.

Features
• They are important financial control devices in Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Policy Cut → amount reduced to Re. 1.
• Economy Cut → amount reduced by a specified amount.
• Token Cut → amount reduced by Rs. 100.

PYQ Trap
• Cut Motions are used only in Lok Sabha because financial control over executive is primarily exercised there.

SIGNIFICANCE

Significance
• Parliamentary devices ensure ministerial accountability.
• They make the executive answerable to the legislature.
• They strengthen deliberative democracy and transparency.

Conclusion
• Parliamentary devices are the operational tools of legislative control over the executive.
• They are essential for the healthy functioning of India’s parliamentary democracy.
Polity.Types of Bills:
TYPES OF BILLS

Introduction
• Bills are proposals for new laws or amendments to existing laws placed before Parliament.
• After passing both Houses and receiving President’s assent, a Bill becomes an Act.

Important Points
• Bills are classified based on their content and procedure.

PYQ Trap
• All Bills become Acts only after President’s assent.

ORDINARY BILLS

Features
• Deal with matters other than financial matters.

Important Points
• Can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
• Must be passed by both Houses.

PYQ Trap
• Joint sitting is possible in case of deadlock.

MONEY BILL

Features
• Defined under Article 110.

Important Points
• Deals exclusively with taxation, borrowing, Consolidated Fund etc.
• Can be introduced only in Lok Sabha.
• Prior recommendation of President required.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker of Lok Sabha certifies whether a bill is Money Bill.

ROLE OF RAJYA SABHA IN MONEY BILL

Features
• Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend.

Important Points
• Can only recommend changes.
• Must return within 14 days.

PYQ Trap
• If not returned within 14 days → deemed passed.

FINANCIAL BILLS

Features
• Contain financial provisions but not strictly Money Bills.

Important Points
• Two types:
  – Financial Bill (Category I) → Similar to Money Bill but includes other matters
  – Financial Bill (Category II) → Involves expenditure from Consolidated Fund

PYQ Trap
• Financial Bills require President’s recommendation but follow ordinary bill procedure.

CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT BILLS

Features
• Amend provisions of Constitution.

Important Points
• Governed by Article 368.
• Can be introduced in either House.

PYQ Trap
• No joint sitting allowed.

PRIVATE MEMBER BILL

Features
• Introduced by a member who is not a minister.

Important Points
• Very few become law.

PYQ Trap
• Most bills passed are Government Bills.

GOVERNMENT BILL

Features
• Introduced by ministers.

Important Points
• Reflect government policy.

DIFFERENCE BETWEEN MONEY BILL AND FINANCIAL BILL

Important Points
• Money Bill → only financial matters (Article 110).
• Financial Bill → broader scope including non-financial provisions.

PYQ Trap
• All Money Bills are Financial Bills, but not all Financial Bills are Money Bills.

SIGNIFICANCE

Significance
• Bills are essential for law-making.
• Classification ensures proper legislative procedure.

Conclusion
• Different types of bills ensure flexibility and specialization in legislative functioning.
• Understanding their procedure is crucial for parliamentary accountability.
Polity.Speaker and Deputy Speaker (Lok Sabha):
SPEAKER AND DEPUTY SPEAKER (LOK SABHA)

Introduction
• The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha and the guardian of its powers, privileges and proceedings.
• The Deputy Speaker assists and performs duties in absence of the Speaker.

Important Points
• Articles 93–97 deal with Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker is not subordinate to the executive; he is an independent constitutional authority.

ELECTION

Features
• Elected by Lok Sabha from among its members.

Important Points
• Usually elected in the first sitting of newly constituted Lok Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Not appointed by President.

TENURE

Features
• Holds office during the life of Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Continues even after dissolution until new Speaker is elected.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker continues after dissolution (important fact).

REMOVAL

Features
• Removed by resolution of Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Requires majority of all members present and voting.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker cannot preside during removal proceedings.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Presides over Lok Sabha proceedings.
• Maintains order and discipline.

Important Points
• Decides admissibility of questions and motions.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker’s rulings are final in procedural matters.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill.

Important Points
• Certification is final and cannot be challenged in court.

PYQ Trap
• Money Bill decision = exclusive power of Speaker.

DISCIPLINARY POWERS

Features
• Can suspend or expel members.

ANTI-DEFECTION POWERS

Features
• Decides disqualification of members under Tenth Schedule.

Important Points
• Decision subject to judicial review.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker’s decision not absolute (subject to court review).

ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS

Features
• Heads Lok Sabha Secretariat.

Important Points
• Controls business of House.

VOTING POWERS

Features
• Does not vote in first instance.
• Exercises casting vote in case of tie.

PYQ Trap
• Casting vote only in case of equality of votes.

DEPUTY SPEAKER

Features
• Elected by Lok Sabha.

Important Points
• Presides in absence of Speaker.

PYQ Trap
• Deputy Speaker does not have independent authority like Speaker.

INDEPENDENCE OF SPEAKER

Features
• Salary charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
• Security of tenure.

Important Points
• Expected to act impartially.

SIGNIFICANCE

Significance
• Ensures smooth functioning of Lok Sabha.
• Maintains discipline and order.
• Protects democratic process.

Conclusion
• The Speaker is a key constitutional authority ensuring neutrality and efficiency in parliamentary proceedings.
• The Deputy Speaker supports continuity of legislative functioning.
Polity.Chairman and Deputy Chairman (Rajya Sabh:
CHAIRMAN AND DEPUTY CHAIRMAN (RAJYA SABHA)

Introduction
• The Chairman is the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha.
• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.
• The Deputy Chairman performs functions in absence of the Chairman.

Important Points
• Articles 89–92 deal with Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

PYQ Trap
• Chairman of Rajya Sabha is not elected by the House separately; he is the Vice-President.

CHAIRMAN OF RAJYA SABHA

Features
• Ex-officio Chairman = Vice-President of India.

Important Points
• Not a member of Rajya Sabha.

PYQ Trap
• Chairman is not a member of the House.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Presides over proceedings of Rajya Sabha.
• Maintains order and discipline.

Important Points
• Decides admissibility of motions and questions.

PYQ Trap
• Similar to Speaker but without Money Bill certification power.

VOTING POWERS

Features
• Does not vote in first instance.
• Has casting vote in case of tie.

PYQ Trap
• Chairman has casting vote like Speaker.

LIMITATIONS

Important Points
• Cannot decide Money Bill status.

PYQ Trap
• Only Speaker has authority to certify Money Bill.

DEPUTY CHAIRMAN

Features
• Elected by Rajya Sabha from among its members.

Important Points
• Presides in absence of Chairman.

PYQ Trap
• Deputy Chairman is a member of Rajya Sabha.

REMOVAL OF DEPUTY CHAIRMAN

Features
• Removed by resolution of Rajya Sabha.

Important Points
• Requires majority of members present and voting.

PYQ Trap
• Chairman (VP) removed differently (as Vice-President under Article 67).

PANEL OF VICE-CHAIRMEN

Features
• Panel members preside in absence of Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

SIGNIFICANCE

Significance
• Ensures orderly functioning of Rajya Sabha.
• Maintains parliamentary discipline.

Conclusion
• The Chairman and Deputy Chairman are essential for functioning of Rajya Sabha.
• They ensure smooth legislative proceedings and uphold parliamentary traditions.
Polity.Supreme Court:
SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

Introduction
• The Supreme Court is the highest judicial authority in India.
• It is the guardian of the Constitution and protector of Fundamental Rights.

Important Points
• Established under Article 124.

PYQ Trap
• Supreme Court = guardian of Constitution (frequently asked).

COMPOSITION OF SUPREME COURT

Features
• Chief Justice of India + other judges.

Important Points
• Strength decided by Parliament.

PYQ Trap
• Number of judges is not fixed in Constitution.

APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Based on Collegium System (judicial evolution).

PYQ Trap
• Collegium not mentioned in Constitution.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Judge of High Court for 5 years OR
• Advocate of High Court for 10 years OR
• Distinguished jurist.

TENURE

Features
• Judges hold office till 65 years of age.

REMOVAL OF JUDGES

Features
• Removed by impeachment by Parliament.

Important Points
• Grounds → proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

PYQ Trap
• Removal requires special majority in both Houses.

JURISDICTION OF SUPREME COURT

ORIGINAL JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 131 → Centre-State disputes.

APPELLATE JURISDICTION

Features
• Appeals from High Courts in civil, criminal and constitutional cases.

WRIT JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 32 → Enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

PYQ Trap
• Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.

ADVISORY JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 143 → President can seek advice.

PYQ Trap
• Advice is not binding on President.

JUDICIAL REVIEW

Features
• Power to examine constitutionality of laws.

PYQ Trap
• Judicial Review = Basic Structure.

JUDICIAL ACTIVISM AND PIL

Features
• Public Interest Litigation allows access to justice.

Important Points
• Relaxation of locus standi.

PYQ Trap
• PIL expanded scope of Article 21.

IMPORTANT DOCTRINES

Features
• Basic Structure Doctrine.
• Doctrine of Judicial Review.

PYQ Trap
• Basic Structure evolved in Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• Kesavananda Bharati → Basic Structure.
• Maneka Gandhi → Expanded Article 21.
• NJAC Case (2015) → Collegium upheld.

PYQ Trap
• NJAC declared unconstitutional.

INDEPENDENCE OF JUDICIARY

Features
• Security of tenure.
• Fixed service conditions.
• Separation from executive.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Protects Fundamental Rights.
• Ensures constitutional supremacy.
• Maintains federal balance.

Conclusion
• The Supreme Court plays a vital role in safeguarding democracy.
• It ensures rule of law and constitutional governance.
Polity.High Court:
HIGH COURT

Introduction
• The High Court is the highest judicial authority at the State level.
• It acts as a guardian of Fundamental Rights within its territorial jurisdiction.

Important Points
• Articles 214–231 deal with High Courts.

PYQ Trap
• Every State has a High Court, but one High Court can serve multiple States.

COMPOSITION OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Chief Justice and other judges.

Important Points
• Number of judges determined by the President.

PYQ Trap
• Strength not fixed in Constitution.

APPOINTMENT OF JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Consultation with Chief Justice of India and Governor.
• Collegium system followed (judicial evolution).

PYQ Trap
• Collegium not mentioned in Constitution.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• At least 10 years judicial office OR advocate of High Court for 10 years.

TENURE

Features
• Judges hold office till 62 years.

PYQ Trap
• HC retirement age = 62 (SC = 65).

REMOVAL

Features
• Same procedure as Supreme Court judges.

Important Points
• Removal by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

JURISDICTION OF HIGH COURT

ORIGINAL JURISDICTION

Features
• In certain civil and criminal matters.

WRIT JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 226 → Can issue writs.

Important Points
• Wider than Supreme Court (Article 32).

PYQ Trap
• HC can issue writs for FR and other legal rights.

APPELLATE JURISDICTION

Features
• Appeals from subordinate courts.

SUPERVISORY JURISDICTION

Features
• Article 227 → Superintendence over subordinate courts.

PYQ Trap
• Supervisory power unique feature of High Court.

COURT OF RECORD

Features
• Can punish for contempt of court.

TRANSFER OF JUDGES

Features
• President can transfer judges from one HC to another.

Important Points
• Consultation with Chief Justice of India.

INDEPENDENCE OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Security of tenure.
• Fixed service conditions.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Protects rights at State level.
• Ensures judicial control over administration.

Conclusion
• The High Court plays a vital role in maintaining rule of law at the State level.
• It acts as a bridge between Supreme Court and subordinate judiciary.
Polity.Subordinate Courts:
SUBORDINATE COURTS

Introduction
• Subordinate Courts operate below the High Courts and handle civil and criminal cases at district and local levels.
• They form the base of the judicial pyramid in India.

Important Points
• Articles 233–237 deal with Subordinate Courts.

PYQ Trap
• Subordinate Courts are under control of High Courts.

STRUCTURE OF SUBORDINATE COURTS

Features
• District Courts
• Sessions Courts (criminal)
• Civil Courts (District Judge, Civil Judge)
• Magistrate Courts

PYQ Trap
• District Judge is highest judicial authority at district level.

APPOINTMENT OF DISTRICT JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by Governor.

Important Points
• Consultation with High Court.

PYQ Trap
• High Court plays key role in appointment.

APPOINTMENT OF OTHER JUDGES

Features
• Appointed by Governor as per rules.

CONTROL OF HIGH COURT

Features
• Article 235 → High Court exercises control over subordinate judiciary.

Important Points
• Includes posting, promotion and discipline.

PYQ Trap
• Control lies with High Court, not State Government.

SEPARATION OF JUDICIARY

Features
• Article 50 → Separation of judiciary from executive.

Important Points
• Ensures independence of judiciary.

JURISDICTION

Features
• Civil and criminal jurisdiction at local level.

IMPORTANT ROLES

Features
• Handling majority of litigation.
• Providing access to justice at grassroots level.

COURTS OF RECORD

Features
• Subordinate courts are not courts of record.

PYQ Trap
• Only Supreme Court and High Courts are courts of record.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures justice delivery at grassroots.
• Reduces burden on higher judiciary.

Conclusion
• Subordinate Courts are essential for effective administration of justice.
• They strengthen the judicial system by ensuring accessibility and efficiency.
Polity.State Legislature:
STATE LEGISLATURE

Introduction
• The State Legislature is the law-making body at the State level.
• It performs legislative, financial and oversight functions within the State.

Important Points
• Articles 168–212 deal with State Legislature.

PYQ Trap
• Some States have unicameral and some have bicameral legislature.

COMPOSITION OF STATE LEGISLATURE

Features
• Governor + Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) + Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad, where applicable).

Important Points
• Unicameral → Only Legislative Assembly.
• Bicameral → Assembly + Council.

PYQ Trap
• Legislative Council is not present in all States.

LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY (VIDHAN SABHA)

Features
• Lower House, directly elected by people.

Important Points
• Maximum strength → 500.
• Minimum strength → 60 (exceptions exist).
• Tenure → 5 years.

PYQ Trap
• Can be dissolved by Governor.

LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL (VIDHAN PARISHAD)

Features
• Upper House, permanent body.

Important Points
• 1/3rd members retire every 2 years.
• Maximum strength → 1/3rd of Assembly.
• Minimum strength → 40.

PYQ Trap
• Legislative Council cannot be dissolved.

CREATION AND ABOLITION OF LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL

Features
• Parliament can create or abolish Council.

Important Points
• Requires special resolution of State Assembly.

PYQ Trap
• Parliament acts on recommendation of State Assembly.

SPEAKER AND CHAIRMAN

Features
• Speaker presides over Assembly.
• Chairman presides over Council.

Important Points
• Speaker decides Money Bill at State level.

PYQ Trap
• Speaker’s decision is final.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Can make laws on State List and Concurrent List.

Important Points
• In Concurrent List, Union law prevails in conflict.

PYQ Trap
• State Legislature cannot legislate on Union List.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Money Bill introduced only in Legislative Assembly.

Important Points
• Council has limited role.

PYQ Trap
• Legislative Council cannot reject Money Bill.

CONTROL OVER EXECUTIVE

Features
• Question Hour, motions and discussions.

Important Points
• Council of Ministers responsible to Assembly.

PYQ Trap
• Executive accountable only to Assembly, not Council.

SIGNIFICANCE

Significance
• Represents people at State level.
• Ensures accountability of State executive.

Conclusion
• State Legislature plays a crucial role in federal governance.
• It ensures democratic functioning and accountability at the State level.
Polity.Governor:
GOVERNOR

Introduction
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the State.
• He acts as the nominal executive and representative of the President in the State.

Important Points
• Articles 153–167 deal with Governor.

PYQ Trap
• Governor = agent of Centre in State.

APPOINTMENT OF GOVERNOR

Features
• Appointed by the President.

Important Points
• Not elected.
• Holds office at pleasure of President.

PYQ Trap
• No fixed tenure guarantee (though nominally 5 years).

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Citizen of India.
• Minimum age 35 years.

Important Points
• Cannot be member of Parliament or State Legislature.

TENURE

Features
• Term of 5 years.

PYQ Trap
• Can be removed anytime by President.

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Appoints Chief Minister.
• Appoints Council of Ministers.
• Appoints Advocate General and State officials.

PYQ Trap
• Ministers hold office at pleasure of Governor (but actually CM controlled).

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Summons and prorogues State Legislature.
• Assent to bills.

Important Points
• Can reserve bill for President.

PYQ Trap
• Governor can reserve bill for President (important power).

ORDINANCE POWER

Features
• Article 213 → Can issue ordinance when legislature not in session.

PYQ Trap
• Ordinance has same force as law.

JUDICIAL POWERS

Features
• Can grant pardons, reprieves etc.

Important Points
• Cannot pardon death sentence (unlike President).

PYQ Trap
• Governor cannot pardon death sentence.

DISCRETIONARY POWERS

Features
• Appointment of CM when no clear majority.
• Sending report for President’s Rule.

PYQ Trap
• Discretionary powers not explicitly defined in Constitution.

ROLE IN PRESIDENT’S RULE

Features
• Article 356 → Governor reports failure of constitutional machinery.

PYQ Trap
• Governor’s report basis for President’s Rule.

RELATION WITH CHIEF MINISTER

Important Points
• CM is real executive at State level.
• Governor acts on advice of Council of Ministers.

IMPORTANT JUDGMENTS

Important Points
• SR Bommai Case (1994) → Limited misuse of Article 356.
• Nabam Rebia Case (2016) → Limits on Governor’s discretionary powers.

PYQ Trap
• Governor’s power not absolute.

SIGNIFICANCE

Important Points
• Ensures constitutional governance in State.
• Acts as link between Centre and State.

Conclusion
• The Governor is a constitutional head with limited real powers.
• Functions largely on advice of the Council of Ministers, with some discretionary powers.
Polity.Chief Minister:
CHIEF MINISTER

Introduction
• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of the State.
• He leads the Council of Ministers and governs the State administration.

Important Points
• Articles 163 and 164 deal with Chief Minister and Council of Ministers at State level.

PYQ Trap
• Real executive at State level = Chief Minister (not Governor).

APPOINTMENT OF CHIEF MINISTER

Features
• Appointed by the Governor.

Important Points
• Leader of majority party in Legislative Assembly is appointed.
• In case of no clear majority → Governor exercises discretion.

PYQ Trap
• CM must prove majority in Legislative Assembly.

QUALIFICATIONS

Features
• Must be a member of State Legislature.

Important Points
• If not a member → must become MLA/MLC within 6 months.

PYQ Trap
• CM can be from Legislative Council also.

POSITION AND ROLE

Features
• Head of State government.
• Leader of Legislative Assembly.
• Principal advisor to Governor.

PYQ Trap
• Governor acts on advice of CM and Council of Ministers.

POWERS AND FUNCTIONS

EXECUTIVE POWERS

Features
• Recommends appointment of ministers.
• Allocates portfolios.
• Can recommend removal of ministers.

PYQ Trap
• Ministers hold office at pleasure of Governor but actually controlled by CM.

LEGISLATIVE POWERS

Features
• Leader of House in Assembly.
• Controls legislative agenda.

Important Points
• Advises Governor on summoning and dissolution.

PYQ Trap
• CM influences legislative functioning significantly.

ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS

Features
• Coordinates work of departments.
• Chairs meetings of Council of Ministers.

FINANCIAL POWERS

Features
• Plays key role in budget preparation through Council of Ministers.

RELATION WITH GOVERNOR

Important Points
• Acts as link between Governor and Council of Ministers.
• Communicates decisions of Council to Governor.

PYQ Trap
• Governor normally bound by advice of CM.

COUNCIL OF MINISTERS

Features
